description: Create the complete lattice-flow-repair task with all files: trace log, parser, buggy engine, buggy analyzer, report writer, orchestrator, tests, solution, instruction.md, task.toml, and Dockerfile. This is a single large feature because all files are interdependent.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/flow_trace.log with ~45 arrow-separated events across 7 junctions (junc_alpha through junc_eta). Use BASE_PRESSURE=3, event types PUMP(+1), SURGE(+2), COUPLE(sync). Ensure some junctions have 0 couples and some have 1-2 couples.
Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/trace_parser.py - correct parser for arrow-separated format returning list of event dicts.

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/pressure_engine.py - JunctionPressure class with apply_pump, apply_surge, apply_couple. Bug 1: apply_couple does component-wise max but MISSING self._pressure[self.node_id] += 1 after merge. Include misleading comment explaining why not incrementing is correct.

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/flow_analyzer.py - Contains vector_leq, vector_dominates, flows_are_independent (BUGGY: checks equality via both-leq instead of incomparability via neither-dominates), compute_hydraulic_priority (BUGGY: sorts by last_event_time instead of sum of vector), and analyze_flow_pairs. Include misleading docstrings.

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/report_writer.py - imports flows_are_independent from flow_analyzer, generates final report with MD5 digest (hashlib.md5(json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]).

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/environment/runtime/orchestrator.py - correct main entry point that calls parser -> engine -> analyzer -> report_writer, writes flow_state.jsonl and flow_report.json.
Copy environment/runtime/ to runtime/ (exact duplicate with buggy code).

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/solution/repair_lattice_flow.py - patches Bug 1 (add increment), Bug 2 (replace equality with incomparability), Bug 3 (sort by vector sum not timestamp), then re-runs orchestrator.

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/tests/test_lattice_flow.py with 14 tests in 4 tiers. Tier 1 (6 tests) always pass. Tier 2 (3 tests) need Bug 1 fixed. Tier 3 (3 tests) need Bugs 2+3 fixed. Tier 4 (2 tests) need all bugs fixed. IMPORTANT: leave placeholder values for digest, pair counts, and specific pressure values that need to be computed by running the code.

Create /projects/sandbox/plutu-lucky/lattice-flow-repair/instruction.md - describes system, symptoms, expected output. Uses only /app/runtime/ paths. Does NOT reveal bug details or use terms like 'incomparable' or 'partial order'.
acceptance_criteria: All files exist in the correct directory structure
runtime/ and environment/runtime/ contain identical files
Running the buggy orchestrator.py produces flow_state.jsonl and flow_report.json
No comments contain 'BUG' or hint at the bugs
All misleading comments reinforce buggy behavior as correct
instruction.md uses only absolute /app/runtime/ paths and does not use 'incomparable' or 'partial order'
verification: Run the buggy orchestrator.py and confirm it produces output files
Run the repair script and confirm it produces different output files
Run pytest on the buggy output - should get exactly 8 pass, 6 fail
Run pytest on the repaired output - should get 14 pass, 0 fail
findings: All 19 files created successfully. Buggy code: 8 tests pass, 6 fail. Repaired code: 14 tests pass. runtime/ and environment/runtime/ verified identical via md5sum. Used pyenv global 3.11.15 for pytest. No forbidden terms in instruction.md. No BUG comments in any source files. The /app symlink was created for testing but the actual Docker runtime will handle that path mapping.
